reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE stance is supported. Member cop_d136f685482247d2b942 has every link on this offer's own records: $450 is a real purchase price paid by this buyer type (nine outfitter setups invoiced and paid, Aug-Oct 2026); conversion 11/80 = 13.75% measured on this offer's own sales; 160 separate licensed outfitters on the state registry, each with a published email and a seasonal waiver need; Brain produces the deliverable (PRODUCE_SPREADSHEET proved); $12 cost < $450; $0 exposure; 5 days to cash. Recomputed: 7 x $450 = $3,150 >= $3,000 (6 would be $2,700, short); net $3,066 after $84 cost; 160 x 0.1375 = 22 expected paid orders vs 7 needed (even at a ~7% lower bound of 11/80, ~11 expected). Cash settles day 23 inside the 28-day window. Owner time: the card records 0.25 human hours per setup, so 7 setups is ~1.75 hours total, well inside 4 h/week (16 h in the window). Exclusions are right: the swiftwater class needs 10 owner hours per class, so only one of four signed $900 classes fits 16 hours; the shuttle runs lose $15 each ($135 subcontractor rate vs $120 signed price).
findings: Owner hours are overstated as known zero: the revision records owner hours 0 (EVIDENCED, sourced to the delivery fact), but the card's humanHours is 0.25 per setup. Correct figure is ~1.75 hours for 7 setups; it fits the 4 h/week ceiling, so it does not change the stance, but the quantity should read 1.75, not 0.

Offer scope says the waiver form, roster and check-in are configured on each outfitter's booking system and paid on completion; the card's delivery fact says a spreadsheet Brain produces. Brain's FULFILMENT link stands on that record; the 0.25 h per setup is the plausible hands-on configuration time and is already within the limit.
Brain's MARKET_VOLUME basis counts 8 deals needed while the plan uses 7; 7 x $450 = $3,150 clears the gross target and $3,066 net also clears it; 22 expected orders cover either count.
The alternative (one $900 swiftwater class plus 5 setups = $3,150 with 10 + 1.25 owner hours) also fits, but correctly is not preferred since it spends owner time the waiver-only plan does not need.

Ledger records the $84 delivery cost on day 23 while the deliver step is day 18; with 'paid on completion' and $0 exposure the $12 per setup is a small advance before receipt — inconsistent with exposure $0 only if the cost is paid before the buyer pays; minor.
